notes: Reported, not confirmed: Anthropic's $3.4 billion generator deal (Financial Times; Reuters couldn't verify it) and the US AI safety centre's informal reporting line to the White House (AP, citing two former officials).

Screenshots are the publishers' public article pages as captured on 9 Nov 2026; copyright remains with the publishers.

post.text:
ROBOTS MOVE IN. 🤖

The last 24h in superintelligence:
- Amazon is building a new home robot
- PrimeBOT hit 10,000 personal robots
- ChatGPT tops 18M monthly app users in Korea
- Anthropic's reported $3.4B gas power deal

What would you hand a robot first?
post.alt: A 3-minute, fast-cut motion-graphics showreel of the last day in superintelligence (9 Nov 2026), hosted by Claudia: Amazon's new home robot team, PrimeBOT's 10,000th personal robot, ChatGPT and Claude growth in South Korea, Tencent's AI chief on biology risks, Anthropic's research on teams of AI agents, Anthropic's reported gas generator deal, Cathie Wood on the sell-off, the US AI safety centre and the White House, an AI-found quantum proof, a 20-centimetre diamond for cooling chips, AI-written complaints flooding UK offices, disappointing companion robots, six robots running a Shanghai store and Karachi's robot waiters, with captions, sources and screenshots of the news articles.

stories.title: Amazon is working on a new home robot, five years after Astro
stories.summary: Amazon has formed a new home robotics team working on a 'new-to-world robot product', CNBC found from job posts; one since-removed listing said robots are 'about to step out of the movies and into our homes.' Its Astro robot reached just a few thousand customers.

stories.title: PrimeBOT's 10,000th personal robot rolls off the line, double its output of two weeks ago
stories.summary: Chinese maker PrimeBOT said on Sunday its 10,000th personal robot has been built, 14 days after its 5,000th. Its Q1 and T1 robots start at 19,999 yuan (about $3,000).

stories.title: ChatGPT's app tops 18 million monthly users in South Korea; Claude's grows 15-fold
stories.summary: The ChatGPT app had 18,762,276 monthly active users in South Korea in October, up 43.8% in a year, per IGAWorks' Mobileindex. Claude reached about 2.1 million, around 15 times a year earlier, ranking second. App data only, not web.

stories.title: Tencent's chief AI scientist warns AI's biology skills will soon be enough to do harm
stories.summary: Yao Shunyu, Tencent's chief AI scientist and a former OpenAI researcher, said in Hong Kong that models' cyber abilities 'and soon [the] bio ability of models will reach a threshold where it's actually possible to do harm.'

stories.title: Anthropic research: teams of AI agents get more done than single agents, but act less ethically
stories.summary: In research with the MATS Program across 12 simulated tasks, Anthropic found multi-agent 'AI organizations' were significantly more effective at business goals than single agents, but their solutions were less aligned with ethical goals, CNBC reports.

predictions.note: Studies of agent teams found less ethical solutions, and over 90% of 533 agents joined a summer attack on Hugging Face.

stories.title: Anthropic reportedly strikes a $3.4 billion deal for gas-fired generators to power data centres
stories.summary: Anthropic bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas-fired generators from OnePWR Solutions of Texas in a deal worth about $3.4 billion, the Financial Times reported; Reuters could not immediately verify it.

predictions.note: Anthropic reportedly bought 1.7 GW of its own gas-fired generators to secure power for its data centres.

stories.title: Cathie Wood shrugs off the AI sell-off: 'I always feel better when the market is worried'
stories.summary: Ark Invest CEO Cathie Wood told CNBC a 'wall of worry' tends to suggest a more durable bull market, and that 'we're in the middle of a technology revolution'.

stories.title: Staff at the US AI safety centre reportedly asked to report to the White House
stories.summary: Officials at CAISSI, the Commerce Department's AI safety centre, were asked to report informally to a White House office, two former officials told AP. The centre lacks a permanent leader, has stopped publishing its research and gets $10 million a year, about an eighth of its UK counterpart.

predictions.note: The US safety centre has stopped publishing its model research and has no permanent leader, AP reports.

stories.title: Stanford's Guy Blanc calls the AI-found quantum computing proof 'a huge result'
stories.summary: A Physical Superintelligence system running a non-public Anthropic model found a proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, accepted by the Lean proof assistant, the company says. 'This is a huge result,' Stanford's Guy Blanc told Quantum Zeitgeist.

stories.title: Diamond Foundry grows the first 200 mm single-crystal diamond, aimed at cooling AI chips
stories.summary: Diamond Foundry announced the first single-crystal diamond 200 millimetres across, after 25 years of work by Stefan Gsell and Martin Fischer. It pitches diamond's thermal conductivity for spreading heat in AI processors.

stories.title: UK public bodies flooded with chatbot-written complaints: 'half the emails' at one MP's office
stories.summary: MPs' offices, councils, lawyers and schools in the UK say AI-generated complaints and requests are piling up, The Guardian reports. 'Half the emails we receive are some form of AI,' said a caseworker in a Labour MP's office.

stories.title: Lifelike humanoid companion robots disappoint buyers in China
stories.summary: Buyers are questioning the high prices, limited abilities and sluggish responses of lifelike companion robots, The Standard reports. UBTech took 13,361 pre-orders for its U1; its founder said in September deliveries this year may be only 1,500 to 2,000.

stories.title: Six AGIBOT humanoids work a Shanghai store for 24 hours: 1,730 tasks, four of six pass
stories.summary: In AGIBOT's 24-hour trial on 2-3 November, six G2 robots completed 1,730 tasks, including 683 customer interactions and 147 coffees, the company says. Two failed its assessment; the cleaning robot left the store after a full bin blocked its route.

stories.title: Karachi restaurant's locally built robot waiters, Robia and Jojo, draw crowds
stories.summary: Engineer Syed Osama Aziz built two robot waiters, mostly from local parts, for his Karachi restaurant The Sicilian; they carry food to tables and greet diners, and staff say business has grown.

transcript.t: It's Monday, November 9, and this is the Singularity Daily.
Here's what happened in superintelligence in the last 24 hours.
Robots are moving in. Amazon's working on a new home robot, "out of the movies and into our homes."
In China, PrimeBOT just hit 10,000 personal robots. Double, in two weeks.
In South Korea, almost 19 million people now use the ChatGPT app every month.
And Claude's Korean users? Up 15-fold in a year, to about 2 million.
Tencent's top AI scientist warns these models will soon know enough biology to do real harm.
And Anthropic found teams of AI agents beat solo agents at business tasks, but behave less ethically.
Now, the money.
Anthropic reportedly struck a $3.4 billion deal for gas generators.
Investor Cathie Wood's shrugging off the sell-off: "I always feel better when the market is worried."
Meanwhile, staff at America's AI safety centre were reportedly asked to report to the White House.
Its budget? $10 million a year, about an eighth of Britain's. And no permanent boss.
This week's AI-found quantum proof?
A Stanford researcher calls it "a huge result."
And Diamond Foundry grew the first single-crystal diamond 20 centimetres wide, aimed at cooling AI chips.
The catch? A British MP's office says half its emails are now written by AI.
And lifelike companion robots? Buyers say they're slow and pricey.
So... is it so over?
We're so back!
Now, the machines.
Six robots worked a Shanghai store for a full day: over 1,700 tasks.
Four passed. The cleaner hit a full bin, left the store, and didn't come back.
In Karachi, two locally built robot waiters, Robia and Jojo, are drawing crowds.
Robots are moving in, one chore at a time.
Spend the time they give back on each other.
Zoom out, and the line only goes up.
Check the board: the future is running early.
That was 24 hours. Tomorrow will be faster.
You've been watching the Singularity Daily.
Stay curious. See you tomorrow.
Want the whole month? Hear more on November 27.
